function: A PPO agent (MAPPO) sets phase shifts of satellite-borne RISs, jointly with a packet-routing agent, to maximize end-to-end data rate; WOA sets GBS power. pp. 16-17.
system: Multi-hop RIS-assisted LEO satellite network: GBS with K antennas, single-antenna users, passive reflecting RISs on satellites, 0.1 THz carrier, 500 km altitude. pp. 7, 11, 24.
method: Reinforcement learning (MAPPO): PPO actor-critic agents for routing and RIS phase shift, centralized training with distributed execution; K-means and WOA handle association and power. pp. 15-19.
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS-dominated Rician fading with composite sub-THz loss (spreading, molecular absorption, rain and cloud per ITU-R, ionosphere), circular LEO orbits at 500 km. pp. 9-12, 23.
test_conditions: Random RUE and GBS positions each training episode (500000 iterations); results swept over distance, data size, RIS elements; no unseen scenario or test split stated. pp. 20, 24-26.
baselines: Learned: MA-TRPO, MA-A2C, Central single-agent PPO. Others: NonRIS (basic satellite without RIS), Fairness_p (fair GBS power, other variables by proposed method). No random, fixed or optimization baseline. p. 23.
metrics: Reward convergence of the agents, average data rate (Mbps) versus distance and RIS elements, latency versus data size, batch-size ablation. pp. 24-27.
q1_support: p. 12: "we use Rician fading to simulate the" channels. Custom simulator; rain and cloud terms follow ITU-R recommendations (p. 10), but no 3GPP TR 38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 26: "we explore the impact of RISs and their number of elements on the rewards" of the phase-shift agents. Each RIS size has its own learning curve; no trained agent is reported tested on an unseen setting.
q3_support: p. 23: "NonRIS: Instead of using a satellite-based RIS, we only employed a basic satellite to compare the two scenarios". MA-TRPO and MA-A2C are learned baselines, but no non-learned phase-shift or routing method is compared; Fairness_p reuses the proposed approach.
q4_support: p. 3: "a novel and computationally efficient solution mechanism" is a qualitative claim only; Table I (p. 24) lists layer widths but no parameter count, operations or runtime.
q5_support: p. 12: "we use Rician fading to simulate the" channels. The authors' own simulator is used; no code or data link and no public dataset or measured data appear.
notes: Area 6 over 3 by the precedence rule: the learned RIS phase-shift agent controls satellite-borne RIS beams in an NTN link, and the routing agent acts above PHY (pp. 16-17); K-means association and WOA power are not learned. Flags for the reviewer: q1, rain and cloud losses use ITU-R P.618, P.838, P.837 and the ITU-R cloud model (p. 10) but fading is the authors' Rician model; q3, NonRIS (p. 23) is the only non-learned-like reference. PDF is arXiv v1 of 28 Jul 2023 (p. 1) and prints no DOI, so the DOI was not checked against it.
